newDescription:
In this Year 3 English lesson, pupils learn what homophones are and how context helps us choose the correct spelling when two or more words sound the same.

This lesson includes:
✔ Understanding that homophones sound the same but have different meanings and can have different spellings
✔ Using sentence meaning to choose the correct homophone
✔ Comparing common homophone pairs and groups such as see/sea, bare/bear, leek/leak, fir/fur, site/sight, allowed/aloud, ate/eight and ball/bawl
✔ Working with three-way homophone groups such as bye/buy/by, you/yew/ewe and heal/heel/he’ll
✔ Exploring less familiar pairs such as cereal/serial, due/dew, flour/flower, forth/fourth, great/grate, reign/rain, sow/sew and slay/sleigh
✔ Recognising silent letters and contractions where they affect spelling, including knight/night and he’ll/heel/heal
✔ Distinguishing true homophones from near homophones by listening carefully to pronunciation
✔ Applying spelling and vocabulary knowledge through repeated sentence-completion and matching activities

Pupils begin by defining homophones and comparing familiar examples such as see and sea and bare and bear. They then complete a series of sentence-based challenges, using meaning and context to select the correct spelling.

As the lesson progresses, pupils encounter a wide range of increasingly demanding homophone pairs and groups. They are encouraged to explain both spelling and meaning, not simply rely on sound.

The lesson finishes by comparing homophones with near homophones, helping pupils listen carefully for small sound differences as well as recognising words that sound exactly alike.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to identify homophones, select the correct spelling from context, explain the different meanings of homophone pairs, and distinguish true homophones from similar-sounding words.
